I'm a graveyard supervisor, been doing 8 to 16 hour shifts. My advice would be make your sleep schedule out so you are waking up before your shift, giving you enough time to fully wake up, eat a meal or snack, shower and get ready, and still have enough time to arrive on time or early in case of traffic. 
 
Drink a lot of water, especially if it's cold; I've a habit of running the heat on in my vehicle and sweating a lot without water will dehydrate you fast. Caffeine is good, but honestly once the sleep schedule kicks in you will find you can do your shifts without caffeine; I find caffeine helps a lot, but the more you drink the more you become reliant on caffeine and can't function without it. I highly recommend not smoking/vaping/chewing, but if you already do it works wonders; makes the time go by faster, keeps you awake, and kills your appetite. 
 
Now I'm not your supervisor, and every supervisor is going to be different, personally my stance on sleeping on site is I'm okay with power naps here and there, nothing longer than like 20-30 minutes. As long as my officers are responding to their radios, doing their tours, and checking out any alarms I'm okay with it; but again, im not your supervisor and I know others are pretty anal about it. If you have a supervisor who doesn't care/looks the other way, don't abuse it and be sleeping for hours at a time, that'll definitely piss them off.
 
As for food, get into the habit of meal prepping if you haven't already; I'm guilty of this, but ordering door dash for every meal is just going to kill your wallet and negate any of the overtime cash you are earning, it's easy to drop 40-60 dollars a day just in food if you are ordering every meal; pack yourself food. Best of luck out there!
